phrases.text: Question 2 is about places of worship during a state of emergency.
The 2023 Legislature approved the amendment; the 2025 Legislature approved it again.
Today, the constitution says the right to worship according to conscience shall never be infringed.
The amendment would bar the state and local governments from ordering places of worship closed, or forbidding gatherings there, in response to an emergency.
The rule would cover national, state and local emergencies, including public health emergencies.
Wisconsin's Type A Notice of Referendum does not include a cost estimate for the amendment.
Wisconsin publishes no official argument against the amendment.
Wisconsin publishes no official argument for the amendment.
A yes vote means governments could not close places of worship or forbid gatherings there in an emergency.
A no vote leaves the religious liberty section as it is today.
